title: How to Deploy to the ICP Network
section: 39. Deploying to the ICP Live Blockchain
summary: Deploys the DBank project to the live Internet Computer with dfx deploy --network ic, finds the frontend canister's id to build its public URL, and shows why first deployments cost many cycles while later upgrades are cheap.

concepts.heading: Deploying to the live network
points: Prerequisite: the cycles wallet is funded and linked to the project (previous lecture).
From inside the project folder run npm install first so the frontend packages are present; if already installed it only takes seconds.
Run dfx deploy --network ic. The --network flag selects the ic (Internet Computer mainnet) instead of the default local replica. It can take a few minutes.
The command creates the canisters on the network (paid from the wallet's cycles) and uploads the built frontend assets into the assets canister. It ends by listing the deployed canisters.

concepts.heading: Finding and opening the live site
points: Get the frontend canister's id with dfx canister --network ic id <assets canister name> (dbank_assets in the lecture; dbank_frontend in the newer template/reference repo).
Open https://<canister-id>.ic0.app in a browser. This is a normal public URL that anyone with internet access can use.
Test it by topping up; the calls now run on the real network (the backend query and update calls behave as they did locally, just with real latency).
(Extra) Newer docs also serve canisters on .icp0.io, and a canister id domain works the same way.

concepts.heading: Cycle costs: creating vs upgrading
points: Re-open the cycles wallet page (you may need to log in again): the balance drops noticeably after the first deployment (example: from 14 trillion downwards), because creating a canister is the costliest operation.
Redeploying after editing code (e.g. commenting out two lines in main.mo) prints that all canisters already exist and only upgrades the code. That is far cheaper.
Practical rule: avoid creating new canisters unnecessarily; update existing ones.

code_examples.caption: Deploy to the live Internet Computer and get the site address
code_examples.code:
npm install
dfx deploy --network ic
dfx canister --network ic id dbank_frontend   # prints the frontend canister id
# open https://<canister-id>.ic0.app

task.name: Deploy DBANK to the ICP network
task.starting_point: DBANK project with working local frontend and a funded cycles wallet set via dfx identity --network ic set-wallet.
task.goal: Have the DBank app reachable at a public canister URL.
steps: cd into the project and run npm install.
Run dfx deploy --network ic and wait for the deployed canisters message.
Run dfx canister --network ic id with the frontend (assets) canister name to get its id.
Visit https://<id>.ic0.app and try a top-up.
Check the wallet balance to see the cost of creating the canisters.
Make a small edit and redeploy to see the cheaper upgrade path.
task.expected_result: The live site works like the local one; the first deploy visibly lowers the cycles balance, and the second deploy reports canisters already created.

pitfalls: Omitting --network ic deploys only to the local replica.
Deploying fresh canisters repeatedly burns the free cycles.
Wallet page may require logging in again before showing the balance.
(Extra) Use your own project's frontend canister name when asking for the id.

gaps_and_ideas: Could be folded into a 'Deploying a dapp' concept lesson with a command checklist task (match each command to what it does: npm install, dfx start, dfx deploy, dfx deploy --network ic, dfx canister id) and a flowchart demo of local vs ic deployment.
